_provenance: REAL — live-verified 2026-08-21 against http://172.20.24.228:9000 (TheHive 5.7.5-1), disposable test case ~8609848. Two rounds: (1) raw endpoint discovery probes via httpx, (2) the composed production function tools/thehive.py::add_extracted_observables called for real with all 6 ExtractedObservables buckets populated, then read back through this repo's own _fetch_case_observables and _query helpers. Not hand-written, not synthetic.
_scope: Covers observable CREATION on an existing case. Says nothing about creating observables on an ALERT (different endpoint, never probed) or about bulk creation.
response_shape: A LIST containing the created observable object(s), not a bare object.
endpoint_note: This one was right on the first try, unlike /promote (404) and /api/v1/comment/case/{id} (404) in the earlier write-endpoint discovery round.

composed_function_live_run.input: ExtractedObservables with all 6 buckets populated, 1 item each

_the_finding_that_matters: process and file BOTH map to dataType 'filename' — so the react/malicious tag decision can NOT be derived from dataType. The BUCKET is the only discriminator. The live run above proves the production code gets this right: two observables landed with identical dataType 'filename', and only the one from the process bucket carries ['malicious','react']. A future refactor that switches the tag condition to key off data_type instead of bucket_name would silently tag every file observable as malicious, and this fixture is the evidence that would catch it.
tag_behavior: Tags are stored exactly as sent, but TheHive returns them in a DIFFERENT ORDER than submitted (sent ['react','malicious'], returned ['malicious','react']). Any assertion on tags must sort or use a set — never compare the list positionally.
cleanup_note: The observables created by these runs are still on test case ~8609848 (values all contain 'soc3s-test' or 'soc3s-live-check', plus 203.0.113.77 which is TEST-NET-3 and non-routable by RFC 5737). Safe to delete; harmless if left.
